the name of the tutorial (only appears in menu). Describes the area where the player arrives on the coast of the Island of Entacca.
Entacca is a made up proper noun that describes the island's role as the mantid's world & birthplace.

the name of the Tuning Court, which is the first arena in the tutorial. This is where the original crafters of the boomerang "tuned" the weapon, like an instrument. The arena is surrounded by taught strings which emit notes when hit. Musical connotation intended to invoke the "tuning" or perfection of the boomerang.

the name of the Composer's Garden, which is the second arena in the tutorial. This is where the boomerang's "composer" (the creature/person that built the boomerang's form) kept a garden for relaxation and meditation. Musical connotation is intended, as though the boomerang were a piece of music.

the name of level 1. A clearing at the edge of the mantids' kingdom in the Yoranwood. This is the place that Kenak (A Julius Caesar-type who united the mantid hives for a time) was exiled and forced to leave the island. A statue depicts them looking forlornly back at the gates to the Yoranwood.
name of the area between levels 1 and 2. This is where you will get the flux upgrade.
the name of level 2. This is a sporting arena where warriors from the different hives would fight in order to settle disputes. Created after Kenak's rise to replace warfare between hives.

name of the area between levels 2 and 3. This is the first "Rest Stop", and the first place the Millipede (Tepan) appears. It is a shrine to a mantis god/mythical figure Kaspidae, who performed magic through music.

english: THE VALLEY OF THE FIRST NYMPHS
context: the name of the pre-level before level 3. This is a farm inside an old castle, surrounded by more farmland. This is the place the mantids believe their kind first arrived on the island. A "nymph" is a young mantis.
the name of level 2. This is an ancient forest that acts as a central neutral ground for each of the Yoran Hives. It is the focal point of mantid civilization.

name of the area between levels 3 and 4. This is the second "Rest Stop" where the millipede is. The mantids buried here are said to be directly descended from Kaspidae and are more magical that usual mantids. They are buried together here when they die, and small seeds are planted in their bodies.

the name of the pre-level before level 4. This is the first of the locations inside the Starved Hive. During the war, Kenak cut off the food supply to this resistant hive as a warning to the other hives. Much of this hive's culture was destroyed by Kenak, including its name. At some point the well was poisoned as retribution against anyone who might try to occupy the hive at a later time.

the name of level 4. Once the main confluence for sewage & water throughout the Starved Hive, in the years after the hive's decimation a massive subterranean worm entered the cavern and created a nest for its young. This is the same worm whose carcass is found in Atsil's Quarry.

name of the area between levels 4 and 5. The third "rest stop" where Tepan appears. This was the central meeting place for the leaders of the Starved Hive before Kenak destroyed it. In the present day, it was used as a place to construct a prototype weapon to fight the goo that wasn't finished in time.

name of the pre-level before level 5. The cave where the mantids first found the crystals and began mining them after the re-opening of the Starved Hive. It is still used off and on, but the bulk of the mining operations have moved further downwards.

the name of level 5. The inside of a giant, frozen worm carcass. This worm long terrorized the miners digging for crystals. The leader of these miners, named Atsil, took water from the poisoned well and fed it to the worm, killing it. The miners then harvested its bones and ate its meat as a delicacy.
name of the area between levels 5 and 6. The fourth "rest stop" where Tepan appears. These baths are part of a subterranean palace built for a misanthropic hermit mantis.

name of the area between levels 4 and 5. A dining hall built for the Hermit, where they would stage mock feasts with mantid statues. Now almost completely destroyed following the flight from the Bastion.

english: THE GRAVE OF THE YORAN LEGION
context: the name of level 5. A hurriedly constructed fortress built by the hastily put together Yoran Legion. This group of warriors, used to fighting in the Grudge Pits, were unprepared to fight as an army and were quickly overrun by the goo creatures.

name of the area between levels 5 and 6. The Fifth and final "rest stop" where Tepan appears, the largest and most central mine where the crystals were harvested. It was here that somehow the goo was released from the crystals and wiped out the Yoran mantids.

the name of level 6. This is a partially supernatural place where The Tree resides. This tree connects the mantid world to many other realities, and is how Tepan arrived on the island. It is a sacred place to the Yoran, but also a terrifying curiosity. The goo has since gotten into the tree, and is blocking Tepan's way home.

the name of level 7. This is a place beyond the reality of the rest of the game, accessed through the tree. Here, the primary form of goo resides, attempting to break out into other worlds. The catalyst for the goo's release was when a Descendent of Kaspidae touched the greatest of the crystals and suddenly exclaimed "Vashkatar!" before the crystal cracked open and goo flooded out.

english: Ah!|pause| What are you?|pause| You aren't one of the Yoran mantids!|pause| Where have you dropped in from?
polish: Ach!|pause| Czym ty jesteś?|pause| Nie należysz do modliszek Yoran!|pause| Skąd ty się tu bierzesz?
context:
The first time our millipede character, Tepan, first talks to the player. They are surprised to see the player after spending many days alone on the island after the massacre of the Yoran mantids.
Tepan speaks in a stream of consciousness way and will often change grammar in the middle of a sentence as their thoughts change, usually after an ellipses. Tepan has been written as though they are constantly rambling on.
This is my first time having my writing localized, so I'm going to be as specific as possible even about obvious things just to be as helpful as possible to you all. Also many of the characters (Tepan, Kenak) referenced are not gendered, and in english we refer to these characters with "they" pronouns -- if needed, Tepan should be gendered female, and Kenak male.

Also, the |pause|, |long_pause| and |short_pause| keywords are used to time out the scrolling of the dialogue. We generally use |pause| after periods (and exclamation marks, etc), |short_pause| after commas, and |long_pause| after ellipses. These keywords don't count towards the character limit.

"Scattermoss roast" is just a made-up dish. I just imagine Tepan's bug species eat all kinds of strange things, like moss that grows in their world.

context: Tepan laments how quickly the Yoran were destroyed, not even having time to give a name to the goo and it's minions before being completely destroyed.

Tepan is working up the courage to get to the real thing they wish to admit, and states explicitly that they haven't ever seen something be able to get into the portals after them.

polish: Zresztą Yoranom to już chyba wszystko jedno.
context: Regardless of whether or not Tepan brought the creatures in, the Yoran are gone. So Tepan feels a little bad for wanting to be absolved.

english: Ah,|short_pause| what am I doing!|pause| These papers have writing on them,|short_pause| that's what the little lines are!
polish: Ach,|short_pause| co ja wyprawiam!|pause| Na tych papierach jest pismo,|short_pause| te wszystkie kreseczki to właśnie ono!
context: Tepan suddenly realizes the parchment they have been eating is actually mantid records of some kind with possibly important writing on them. Seen as the Yoran are all gone, it's probably not a good idea to consume their culture artifacts.

english: Why would you write on something so tasty?|pause| Alright,|short_pause| well,|short_pause| no more eating the parchment!
polish: Po co pisać na czymś tak smacznym?|pause| No dobrze,|short_pause| już dobrze,|short_pause| koniec z jedzeniem pergaminu!
context:
Tepan is incredulous that the Yoran would use what Tepan considers a meal as a medium for writing. Then, a little dejected, they vow to not eat any more.
Last line of dialogue for this area.

english: Tepan is trying very hard not to eat more paper...
polish: Tepan bardzo się stara nie zjeść więcej papieru...
context: Repeating line that plays after all dialogue has been exhausted, describing what Tepan is doing and why they can no longer talk to the player.

english: There you are!|pause| I saw you down in the worm's carcass!|pause| Launching yourself through the air,|short_pause| slicing and hacking and...|long_pause| Terrifying!|pause| I'm endlessly relieved to see you safe.
polish: Jesteś!|pause| Widać cię było tam, w truchle robaka!|pause| Jak wyrzucasz się w powietrze,|short_pause| tniesz i rąbiesz, i...|long_pause| Przerażające!|pause| Ogromnie mi ulżyło, że nic ci nie jest.
context:
First line of dialogue for the Sauna area. 
Tepan, presumably while travelling from the last rest stop area to this one, finally witnessed the player fighting the goo creatures.
They are surprised and terrified by how the player has been fighting the creatures, and describes a little of what they saw the player doing (slicing, hacking, flying through the air, etc).
Tepan cares for the player character at this point, and is very happy to see them safe once more.

english: The Yoran brought me up through these halls when I first arrived.|pause| The Hermit who lived down here was already long gone by that time.|pause| No one seemed to be able to tell me who they were.
polish: Yoranie prowadzili mnie przez te sale zaraz po moim przybyciu.|pause| Pustelnika, który tu mieszkał, dawno już wtedy nie było.|pause| Nikt nie potrafił mi powiedzieć, kim był.
context:
Tepan recalls their journey up to the surface after emerging from the portal farther below. 
The area the player is in is called the Hermit's Bath, and Tepan mentions that this famous hermit was gone before they arrived on Entacca. None of the Yoran apparently knew much about this hermit, or were unwilling to tell Tepan about it.

english: I would've liked to meet this Hermit,|short_pause| one lonesome soul to another!
polish: Szkoda, że nie doszło do spotkania z tym Pustelnikiem,|short_pause| samotna dusza z samotną duszą!
context: Tepan feels a kinship with the hermit, given that they both live primarily solitary lives (one lonesome soul to another).

english: Still,|short_pause| a strangely ornate place to live alone.|pause| Maybe they were some old hive lord.|pause| Exiled or...
polish: Choć,|short_pause| jak na samotne życie, to dziwnie zdobne miejsce.|pause| Może był jakimś dawnym władcą gniazda.|pause| Wygnanym albo...
context:
Tepan muses about who this hermit might've been, and how they were able to afford and build this seemingly opulent underground home. 
Tepan speculates the hermit might have once been royalty.

english: Or escaping some cruel betrayal!|pause| Maybe they banished all their attendants after it was all built...
polish: Albo uciekającym przed okrutną zdradą!|pause| Może odprawił całą służbę, gdy budowa dobiegła końca...
context: Tepan, now excited, imagines a juicy scenario in which the hermit fled into self-imposed exile after being betrayed by a close friend. Perhaps they sent away all their servants after the underground palace was built and sealed themselves away.

english: Odd that they had all these statues,|short_pause| though.|pause| Maybe they missed people after all.
polish: Dziwne tylko, że trzymał te wszystkie posągi,|short_pause| nie sądzisz?|pause| Może jednak tęsknił za towarzystwem.
context: Tepan thinks maybe the hermit did miss people, and built the statues to remind them of their fellow mantids.

english: I think...|long_pause| just thinking out loud,|short_pause| but I feel a little connection with the Hermit.|pause| I mean,|short_pause| my solitary state wasn't my choice,|short_pause| but the more I think about it...
polish: Myślę sobie...|long_pause| tak głośno myślę,|short_pause| ale czuję z tym Pustelnikiem pewną więź.|pause| To znaczy,|short_pause| moja samotność nie była moim wyborem,|short_pause| ale im dłużej o tym myślę...
context:
Tepan begins speaking, then pauses to think, choosing new words.
Tepan thinks of themselves as similar to this hermit, if only by their shared isolation (the hermit in self-inflicted solitude, and Tepan wandering realities alone).

english: One of the worlds I ended up in...|long_pause| it was...|long_pause| Ah,|short_pause| I don't know how to put this.
polish: Jeden ze światów, do których mnie zaniosło...|long_pause| był...|long_pause| Ach,|short_pause| nie wiem, jak to ująć.
context: Tepan begins recalling an experience they had in one of their visited worlds. The experience had a great impact on them, leaving them shaken. They struggle to find the right words to relate the experience.

english: When I first arrived there,|short_pause| it didn't look like anything in particular.|pause| But the longer I stayed,|short_pause| the more it started to...|long_pause| it tried to shape itself to how I remembered my own home.
polish: Zaraz po przybyciu,|short_pause| nie wyglądał na nic szczególnego.|pause| Ale im dłużej to trwało,|short_pause| tym bardziej zaczynał...|long_pause| próbował ukształtować się tak, jak dom zapisał mi się w pamięci.
context:
Tepan tells of how the world they visited looked unremarkable, but the longer they stayed, the more the environment shifted to resemble places from Tepan's own memory. 
Tepan is clearly still affected by these memories, and is probably having a hard time reliving them.

english: Just the places at first.|pause| A familiar tree,|short_pause| a little market stand...|long_pause| It was amazing to see,|short_pause| especially after all that time.
polish: Najpierw same miejsca.|pause| Znajome drzewo,|short_pause| mały stragan...|long_pause| Niesamowity widok,|short_pause| zwłaszcza po tylu latach.
context: Tepan lists off a few of the things that world created from their memory. At first, Tepan was enthralled by this place and the things it was creating. In a way, Tepan was seeing home again for the first time.

english: But then it started trying to replicate people.
polish: A potem zaczął próbować odtwarzać istoty.
context: Tepan's tone shifts from awe to something more disturbed as they recall when that world tried to recreate the people in Tepan's memories.

english: I spent too long there in the first place.|pause| But one day I returned to what was an approximation of my childhood nest,|short_pause| and I saw...
polish: Nie trzeba było w ogóle tak długo tam zostawać.|pause| Aż pewnego dnia wracam do czegoś, co udawało gniazdo z mojego dzieciństwa,|short_pause| i widzę...
context: Tepan admits to being seduced by this world resembling their own, but remembers the particular event that convinced them to leave.

english: It was trying to make someone I knew.|pause| So next time the portal opened I got me and my hundred legs right out of there!
polish: Próbował ulepić kogoś znajomego.|pause| Więc gdy tylko portal znów się otworzył: w nogi — wszystkie sto — i precz stamtąd!
context:
Tepan clearly remembers the person that world was trying to recreate, but does not share this with the player. 
Horrified by this grotesque being, and realizing Tepan's own thoughts weren't safe from that place, they escaped back through the portal.

english: Well,|short_pause| it's nice to have a real person around again,|short_pause| even if you don't talk much!
polish: Cóż,|short_pause| miło znowu mieć obok siebie prawdziwą osobę,|short_pause| nawet jeśli niewiele mówisz!
context:
Tepan shakes themselves from that emotionally distressing state, and express gladness to have met real people in their travels, particularly the player character. 
Tepan makes a joke regarding the fact that they appreciate the player's company, even if the player never talks back.
Final dialogue for this area.

english: Tepan is muttering about the best way to cook rat bones...
polish: Tepan mamrocze coś o najlepszym sposobie na ugotowanie szczurzych kości...
context: A repeating line describing the action Tepan is doing that prevents them from continuing to talk to the player.

english: Hello there,|short_pause| friend.|pause| We're very near to the end now.|pause| Just down below here is where the Yoran found me.
polish: Witaj,|short_pause| bratnia duszo.|pause| Jesteśmy już bardzo blisko końca.|pause| Tam, niżej, znaleźli mnie Yoranie.
context:
Sensing the end to their journey, Tepan is feeling anxious and subdued, but with a small hint of excitement. Tepan is taking the time to reflect before moving on.
Tepan reveals that they were found below this quarry.

english: It's so cold down here.|pause| When I was last here it was far warmer,|short_pause| like the heart of the world was just below our feet.
polish: Ależ tu zimno.|pause| Za ostatnim razem było tu znacznie cieplej,|short_pause| jakby serce świata biło tuż pod naszymi stopami.
context:
Tepan mentions how the space has changed since they first arrived, becoming cold in the absence of the Yoran and the prolonged presence of the goo.
Tepan likens the heat they felt before as feeling like the core of the earth was closely underneath the quarry.

english: Can you see the crystals?|pause| They're all over these caves.|pause| I'm sure you saw some higher up.
polish: Widzisz te kryształy?|pause| Pełno ich w tych jaskiniach.|pause| Na pewno trafiały ci się wyżej.
context:
Tepan draws the player's attention to the large gems present in the space that have been dotted throughout the game. 
Tepan is subdued, having learned that the black goo has actually come from the crystals.

english: There were thousands of mantids mining them in this pit,|short_pause| sending the gems upwards to the hives.|pause| I never thought...
polish: W tym dole wydobywały je tysiące modliszek,|short_pause| a klejnoty szły w górę, do gniazd.|pause| Nigdy by mi nie przyszło do głowy...
context: Tepan never thought to ask the mantids what they did with the crystals, and realizes this as they say the last sentence.

english: You know,|short_pause| I never learned what the Yoran did with these crystals.|pause| I know they provide light,|short_pause| but...|long_pause| well,|short_pause| they must do something else.
polish: Wiesz,|short_pause| do dziś nie wiem, co Yoranie robili z tymi kryształami.|pause| Wiem, że dają światło,|short_pause| ale...|long_pause| cóż,|short_pause| muszą robić coś jeszcze.
context: Tepan, somewhat confounded and a little upset with themselves, believes the gems must have been used for something else beyond their light-giving properties.

english: Maybe they really did just dig them up because they look pretty...
polish: Może naprawdę kopali je tylko dlatego, że ładnie wyglądają...
context: Tepan then flips, realizing that perhaps the only thing that led the Yoran to dig up the gems was greed.

english: Well,|short_pause| whatever the reason,|short_pause| it cost the Yoran everything.|pause| You'll know what I mean when you go down there...
polish: Cóż,|short_pause| jakikolwiek był powód,|short_pause| kosztowało to Yoran wszystko.|pause| Zrozumiesz, gdy tam zejdziesz...
context:
Understanding that the answer to the question is unattainable and probably moot, Tepan concludes that whatever the reasoning the result is decided. 
Tepan ends with a hint for the player to look closer at the gems, which will be oozing the black goo.

english: I've never been so anxious in all my life.|pause| You'd think that,|short_pause| you know,|short_pause| years and years of exploring a treacherous path between realities would've hardened my nerves,|short_pause| but here we are.
polish: Nigdy w życiu nie było we mnie tyle niepokoju.|pause| Wydawałoby się,|short_pause| wiesz,|short_pause| że całe lata wędrowania zdradliwą ścieżką między rzeczywistościami zahartują nerwy,|short_pause| a jednak.
context: A new conversation, Tepan's thoughts return to finally being able to escape Entacca and continue looking for home. They also find a little humor in the fact that despite their cosmic journeys, Tepan is still able to get scared before embarking on these adventures.

english: A hundred legs to rely on and they all betray me with a quiver!
polish: Sto nóg do dyspozycji i wszystkie zdradzają mnie drżeniem!
context: Tepan's way of saying "my legs are shaking".

english: I cannot begin to thank you enough.|pause| I realized,|short_pause| somewhere back there,|short_pause| that you aren't doing this for me in particular,|short_pause| but...|long_pause| Well,|short_pause| from companion to companion I say thank you.
polish: Nie umiem ci się dostatecznie odwdzięczyć.|pause| Dotarło do mnie,|short_pause| gdzieś tam po drodze,|short_pause| że nie robisz tego akurat dla mnie,|short_pause| ale...|long_pause| Cóż,|short_pause| po przyjacielsku: dziękuję.
context:
Tepan, while unaware of Kaspidae's influence on the player character's actions, can sense that the player isn't destroying the goo simply to help Tepan get home. Regardless, it is helping Tepan, for which they give the player gracious thanks.
A little moment of sentimentality, Tepan does feel like they and the player character are companions of sorts.

english: You're the only reason I'm getting this chance to find home again.
polish: Tylko dzięki tobie mam szansę znów odnaleźć dom.
context: Tepan is trying to hide it, but this sentence is full of a lot of emotions. If Tepan had human eyes, I think they would be close to tearing up.

english: And I worry about that.|pause| About home.|pause| Especially after what happened here.|pause| I can't help but wonder if...
polish: I właśnie o to się martwię.|pause| O dom.|pause| Zwłaszcza po tym, co stało się tutaj.|pause| Nie mogę przestać myśleć, czy...
context: Tepan's worrying nature comes back full force, and again causes them to stumble over the right words to describe what they're feeling.

english: If one day I'll walk through a doorway and find my home is just gone.|pause| Or worse yet,|short_pause| bring something back with me!
polish: Czy pewnego dnia przejdę przez drzwi i zastanę dom, którego już nie ma.|pause| Albo, co gorsza,|short_pause| przyniosę coś ze sobą!
context: This is Tepan's true fear, even more than never finding home again. And even though Tepan knows they didn't let the goo into this world, the idea is now firmly ingrained in their mind. Tepan is wrestling with the fact that maybe the best course of action might be to purposefully never return home.

english: Well,|short_pause| I guess you'll take care of that particular part.|pause| If we don't have the chance to meet again,|short_pause| good luck,|short_pause| and I hope you find your own way home.
polish: Cóż,|short_pause| tą akurat częścią chyba zajmiesz się ty.|pause| Jeśli nie będzie nam dane spotkać się jeszcze raz,|short_pause| powodzenia,|short_pause| i oby udało ci się odnaleźć własną drogę do domu.
context:
A joke about the player hopefully killing the goo monster, so that it would be unable to follow Tepan into another world.
A reserved goodbye, Tepan trying to send the player off to the end of the game, trying to hold it together.

english: You sure I can't try and cook you something up before you go?
polish: Na pewno nie mogę ugotować ci czegoś na drogę?
context:
Tepan's sentimentality breaks through. Probably feeling a little useless to the the player, Tepan offers services in what they believe is their best skill: good cooking. A friend trying to help in whatever way they know best.
Last instance of dialogue.
A repeating message describing an action Tepan is performing that stops them being able to continue talking with the player.

Back to basics.

Powrót do podstaw.
